742240201.text: Huh, looks like we meet again, Tailleferre!

742240202.text: #Ah, it's you two! The adventurer and {M#his}{F#her} little assistant. Sorry, I've forgotten your names...

742240203.text: #The name's Paimon, and {M#he's}{F#she's} {NICKNAME}. Thanks for your help last time, by the way — thanks to you, we managed to use a Conch Harp to play ancient music!

742240204.text: Still, what brings you here to Petrichor?

742240205.text: That's what I wanted to ask you — I'm chasing a rumor, but I suppose adventurers like you might already be well ahead of the game.

742240206.text: Rumors? What are you talking about?

742240207.text: Hmm? Don't you know about the big news out of Petrichor lately...?

742240210.text: Huh? What are you... No, no, I'm talking about the rediscovery of the legendary Faded Castle!

742240211.text: The last records of the place are several centuries ago. And here I thought that was what you were here for!

742240212.text: Oh, that... That might've had something to do with us, sure...

742240213.text: In that case, I'm sure you know that the castle once belonged to Boethius, yes? The most important musician in Fontaine's history?

742240214.text: Whether it be the operas he wrote, or the ancient Remurian scores he compiled, his works all have a special place in music history.

742240215.text: Surely, a vast wealth of resources can be found at the castle in which he once lived, each an important relic to us in the Musicians' Association.

742240216.text: As such, I rushed here as soon as I heard the news, trying to secure any important relics before all the adventurers get here.

742240217.text: But I suppose you were one step ahead of me, eh?

742240218.text: (Err, what should we tell her? That Boethius is actually a big baddie, who used all that music to do a whole bunch of evil stuff...?)

742240801.text: The scenery here truly is rather excellent. We order many an instrument from this town every year, but this is my first time visiting.

742240804.text: I'm counting on you, then. I'll wait for you in town in the meantime.

742240901.text: Hmm, this is... Yes, this is indeed "The Flying Outlander." To think that you actually found it...

742240902.text: It can't have been easy, but I was right to put my trust in you, excellent adventurers!

742240903.text: Hehe, thanks! Still, what are you gonna do with the score? Are you gonna perform it at the Opera Epiclese, maybe make a pile of Mora?

742240904.text: Hmm... Making money is important, but I have no intention of keeping this for my own.

742240905.text: This ancient art is part of the common wealth of humanity. As such, I will release "The Flying Outlander" into the public domain once my research is complete.

742240906.text: After all, is not recovering this lost play and filling in a page of history heretofore missing the greater deed to do?

742240910.text: Well then, I suppose I should hurry back. Research and study await!

742240911.text: Ah yes, here's your payment. If chance should allow it, let us meet again!

742240909.text: Of course. Your name will be on the title page for sure!
